note: Non-jeepney transport in Legazpi City: tricycles, padyak, buses, UV Express, taxis and app-based ride-hailing. Jeepney routes live in transport-routes.json and every fare rule lives in transport-fares.json - this file holds what is specific to each mode: who regulates it, where its terminal is, and how to use it. Terminal coordinates come from OpenStreetMap and are drawn as markers on the same map as the jeepney routes.

modes.name: Tricycles & Taxicles
modes.summary: Franchised by the city through the Sangguniang Panlungsod's Transportation Development and Regulation Division. Fares are fixed by the city, not negotiated - check the fare checker above before you pay.

fare.title: City-wide fare
fare.source: Tamang Singil Advocacy Program, City Government of Legazpi
fare.note: Discounted fares apply to students, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, and start from the first kilometre rather than the second.
fare.verifyNote: Individual paradas can have their own matrix set by ordinance. Parada 2A & 3A, below, is set at ₱15.00 under City Ordinance No. 17-0019-2026, so read the matrix posted at the parada you are riding from.

example.title: Example fare matrix — Parada 2A & 3A (Mandarin)
example.note: Parada 2A & 3A has its own ordinance-set matrix, which is why its fares are ₱15.00 rather than the ₱12.00 city-wide base. Each parada has its own colour code and its own matrix; this is the only one we have so far.

modes.name: Padyak (Pedicab)
modes.summary: The pedal-powered pedicab, used for short hops within a barangay. The Tamang Singil Advocacy Program covers tricycles, taxicles and padyak together, so a padyak is charged on the same schedule as a tricycle.

fare.title: City-wide fare
fare.source: Tamang Singil Advocacy Program, City Government of Legazpi
fare.note: Discounted fares apply to students, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, and start from the first kilometre rather than the second.
fare.verifyNote: The Tamang Singil Advocacy Program sets one fare for tricycle, taxicle and pedicab together, so this matches the tricycle schedule exactly.

modes.note: Padyak are not covered by the jeepney routing plan and have no fixed route - they work short trips around a barangay, a market or a terminal.

links.label: Tricycle and pedicab franchise services (SP Secretariat)

modes.name: Buses
modes.summary: Provincial and Manila-bound buses use the Legazpi Grand Central Terminal. Operators set their own schedules and these change often, so we publish the terminals rather than timetables we cannot keep current.

terminals.name: Daraga Bus Station
terminals.role: Buses serving Daraga and points west

modes.note: Provincial bus fares depend on the class of bus - ordinary, aircon, super deluxe or luxury. The fare checker above covers all four. The Grand Central Terminal is also the destination on several jeepney and tricycle routes on this page.

modes.name: UV Express
modes.summary: UV Express vans connect Legazpi with nearby towns and with Naga. Their routes are authorised by LTFRB Region V rather than by the city, so the route list is not ours to publish — but the terminal is mapped.

terminals.name: Legazpi UV Express Terminal
terminals.role: UV Express vans to nearby towns and Naga

modes.note: We have asked LTFRB Region V for the authorised UV Express route list. Until it arrives, this section names the terminal only.

fare.title: Fare per kilometre
fare.source: UV Express Fare Rate Per Kilometer, LTFRB
fare.note: Students, senior citizens and persons with disabilities get a 20% discount.
fare.verifyNote: Use the fare checker above for a specific distance.

modes.name: Taxis
modes.summary: Metered taxis are regulated nationally by LTFRB. The meter should be running from the moment you board - a quoted flat price is not the published fare.

fare.title: Metered fare
fare.note: Students, senior citizens and persons with disabilities get a 20% discount.
fare.verifyNote: Use the fare checker above to work out what a given trip should cost.

modes.note: Complaints about taxi overcharging go to the LTFRB 24/7 hotline 1342, not to the city.

modes.name: Ride-hailing apps
modes.summary: Grab and JoyRide operate here as TNVS. Their apps price dynamically, but LTFRB publishes the flag-down and per-kilometre rates they are required to work from.
modes.note: Availability depends on the operator, not on the city.
